outcome_detail: Suit filed March 12-13, 2025 against the City of Columbia, the Columbia Police Department, and former officer Caleb Hickmon-Payne, seeking unspecified damages. The parallel criminal case against the officer was still active as of October 2025 (additional charges added). No civil resolution reported as of July 2026.
criminal_detail: Caleb Hickmon-Payne surrendered to the South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) on March 12, 2025 and was charged with second-degree assault and battery and common-law misconduct in office over the January 31, 2025 incident. In October 2025, SLED charged him additionally with third-degree criminal sexual conduct and misconduct in office over an alleged September 6, 2024 sexual battery of a different arrestee in his custody. No plea, trial, or conviction reported as of July 2026. He was fired by CPD on February 7, 2025.
incident_date_approx: January 31, 2025 (arrest and transport); related October 2025 criminal charge concerns a September 6, 2024 incident
description: A 30-year-old Columbia woman sued the City of Columbia, the Columbia Police Department, and former patrol officer Caleb Hickmon-Payne in March 2025. The suit says she was wrongfully arrested during a January 31, 2025 traffic stop on a bench warrant that had been vacated on February 22, 2024 but still appeared in the system. According to the complaint, while she was handcuffed in the officer's patrol car en route to the Alvin S. Glenn Detention Center, Hickmon-Payne made sexually explicit comments, offered her a tobacco product in exchange for a sexual act, and sexually assaulted her by touching her inappropriately at a secluded location. An internal investigation found the drive to the jail took 41 minutes instead of roughly 19, and the department fired him on February 7, 2025. He was criminally charged in March 2025 with second-degree assault and battery and misconduct in office, and in October 2025 SLED added charges of third-degree criminal sexual conduct and misconduct in office over an alleged September 2024 assault of another arrestee in his custody.
notes: The October 2025 SLED charges involve a second alleged victim (a September 6, 2024 arrestee); no separate civil lawsuit by that person was found, so no companion record was created.
